preservation: The original independent authorial witness remains unchanged. This reconciliation governs the proposed final key model, not the later blind reviewer's answers.

reconciliations.resolution: Retain the separate prepositional phrase concerning/from that; ðā bȳsena remains accusative object of both infinitives. The original witness 'from this' is a defensible English connection and is not rewritten as though bȳsena were governed by be.

reconciliations.reason: The source editor independently checked selected Cook printed303 / one-based PDF319, Vocabulary s.v. līeg(43), which explicitly gives thunderbolt, levin. A broad flame sense is not needed for this assigned passage.

final_model_units: Every high honor here in the world is surrounded by dangers: the greater the worldly dignities are, the fiercer the dangers are.
Thus we can recognize and understand the examples from this.

The tree, then, which grows in the woodland so that it rises above all the other trees and spreads itself out—when a storm and the strong wind suddenly come on, it is more violently shaken and battered than the rest of the forest.
It is likewise with the high cliffs and crags: when they tower far above the rest of the earth, they then suddenly begin to fall and crash very violently to the earth.

Likewise with the high mountains and hills which stand high above all the earth: nevertheless they suffer the penalty of that supremacy, in that they are often punished and battered by fire from heaven and struck by thunderbolts.
Thus the high powers here in the world collapse and fall and come to ruin, and the riches of this world turn to sorrow, and these earthly wonders come to nothing.
model_limits: Cook qualifies torr as probably crag in this passage; keep the qualification visible.
The passive participles admit defensible English lexical variation while preserving the three coordinated predicates and their heavenly-fire/thunderbolt means.
Modern English pronouns or an understood object may be supplied where idiomatic, without claiming an additional Old English word.
